data.description:
## Problem
`tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_ensures.py::test_mcp_startup_sweeps_before_run` fails intermittently under CI's pytest-randomly (observed on a py3.13 shard: assertion `order == ['ensures','run']` got `['run']`, i.e. run_ensures was never called). It passes in isolation and on other py-version shards (different random seed).

## Root cause
`mcp_server.main()` only calls `run_ensures` when `os.path.isdir(_config.tracker_dir())` (src/rebar/mcp_server.py ~line 717). Under an unlucky test order a sibling test leaves cwd / tracker-dir resolution state such that `tracker_dir()` does not point at an existing dir, so the ensures sweep is silently skipped and only 'run' is recorded. The test relies on ambient cwd/config state the `repo` fixture does not fully isolate.

## Fix direction
Make the test hermetic (chdir into / point config at the fixture's repo within the test, or assert the tracker-dir precondition) OR make main()'s sweep decision independent of ambient cwd. Root-cause the isolation leak; do not paper over with a retry.

## Impact
Not caused by RP-06 code_review/plan_review changes — surfaced while landing RP-06 S3 (change 2047); the failing test is disjoint from those files. Pre-existing latent flake on main affecting concurrent sessions.
data.title: test_fsck_ensures::test_mcp_startup_sweeps_before_run is order-dependent (flaky under pytest-randomly)
